column3: It repeats the command to set the face toward the upright religion and adds the urgency of an irreversible day.
It joins steadfastness with refusing the path of those without knowledge, directly clarifying the focus's closing contrast.
It explicitly turns the face to the Originator in hanif devotion and rejects association.
It closely joins exclusive worship, the upright religion, and the fact that most people do not know.
Its account of originating and repeating creation supplies a limited same-surah backdrop for the divine creation named in the focus.
It distinguishes the Creator from what cannot create, grounding the focus's appeal to God's created order.
It nearly repeats the command to set the face toward religion as a hanif and avoid association.
Diversity of languages and colors as signs for the knowledgeable gives concrete scope to creation without implying a replacement of its order.
It connects surrendering the face to God, doing good, and following Abraham's hanif way.
It links the greater creation of heaven and earth with most people's lack of knowledge.
The brief report of 'Ad denying the messengers does not clarify orientation, fitrah, or the upright religion.
Divine favor and knowledge here do not add to the focus's account of created disposition or direction.
Its recurring conclusion that most people do not know offers only a broad parallel in a resurrection setting.
As the next ayah, it turns the stated orientation into repentance, prayer, reverence, and refusal of association.
The witness to revelation does not materially explain the focus's fitrah or command of orientation.
God's unbroken promise and the same contrast with widespread ignorance illuminate the focus's claim that His creation is not replaced.
As the immediate contrast, it identifies following desire without knowledge as the alternative to the focus's upright orientation.
Naming God as the one who originated Hud supports a creator-centered allegiance, but not the focus's fuller claim.
It calls the divinely set order of time the upright religion, giving a concrete created ordering to that phrase.
The appeal to ancestral custom weakly contrasts with the focus's appeal to God's original formation.
Iblis's comparison of created materials exposes a distorted use of origin, but does not develop fitrah or upright religion.
Its statement that most people do not know is relevant only at the focus's broad closing level.
As the following ayah, it defines the rejected alternative as splitting religion into self-satisfied parties.
The bare statement that God created humanity gives only general support for the focus's creation language.
Turning faces toward a divinely appointed direction provides a practical, though more limited, form of commanded orientation.
Its parable rejects treating dependents as partners and addresses people who reason, preparing the focus's rejection of association.
Joseph's appeal to the Originator and wish to die submitted offers a secondary model of creator-centered devotion.
It shows that straight guidance follows God's direction rather than attachment to a previous orientation.
Guidance to a straight path reinforces the focus's command to maintain an upright direction.
Its direct description of a straight path supports the focus's upright religious course.
Repeatedly turning faces toward one direction illustrates communal constancy, though this specific qiblah material is already covered.
The isolated letters add no usable clarification to the focus.
The fulfilled promise and the sky's rupture do not explain fitrah, religion, or orientation.
The assertion that God's words are not changed is a useful parallel to the focus's non-replacement of divine creation.
God's sustaining command over heaven, earth, and resurrection offers general evidence of an ordered creation.
It distinguishes replacing a revealed sign from changing God's source or knowledge, sharpening the scope of the focus's no-replacement statement.
Its explicit declaration that no change exists in God's established way closely parallels the focus's unchanging divine creation.
It depicts hanif devotion to God without association and makes the loss of that orientation vividly consequential.
Replacement of skins preserves punishment rather than explaining the permanence of the created order.
It unites a straight, upright religion with Abraham's hanif way and rejection of association.
Human emergence from dust is a same-surah creation sign, but adds little after the stronger formation texts.
Humanity's creation in the best proportion offers a concise parallel to fitrah as a given sound formation.
This repeated qiblah instruction adds little beyond the earlier face-orientation cards.
The report of messengers and victory for believers does not develop the focus's central terms.
Abraham's hanif obedience and non-association are relevant but substantially repeat earlier direct parallels.
It defines Abraham as a hanif submitter rather than a partisan identity and rejects association.
Holding fast to God and receiving straight guidance is a general, already-covered counterpart to upright orientation.
The one-pattern account of collective creation and resurrection gives limited support to a coherent divine order.
The qiblah test shows obedience through a changed direction, but is secondary to the focus's creator-grounded orientation.
The wind's benefits and gratitude do not explain the focus's fitrah or upright religion.
Pharaoh's claim that Moses would change religion exposes a hostile misuse of change, but is only indirect evidence.
It identifies the Originator as the one who will guide beyond inherited worship, directly supporting creator-centered orientation.
Creation of spouses and mercy supplies a general sign of divine ordering without clarifying fitrah.
Guidance to a straight path is relevant, but the revelation context adds little beyond earlier path texts.
Its emphatic statement that the religion is surely real reinforces the focus's description of the upright religion.
It commands following a revealed way and not the desires of those without knowledge, directly echoing the focus and its immediate context.
The financial means that sustain social life do not clarify the focus's religious orientation or creation claim.
Deferred judgment at a fixed term does not add to the focus's central meaning.
The account of wind, clouds, and rain does not materially clarify the focus after earlier creation signs.
Guidance to a straight path provides only a concise general parallel already represented above.
Lordship of the Day of Religion gives limited context for the word religion but not its upright, fitrah-based sense.
Rain reviving dead land is a creation sign for people who reason, but remains peripheral to the focus.
It contrasts examples offered to people with comprehension reserved for the knowledgeable, illuminating the focus's many who do not know.
Its refusal to call on another god directly supports the focus's exclusive religious orientation.
Taking desire as a god and losing guidance gives a detailed contrary model to the focus's creator-grounded, knowledgeable direction.
The assertion that God created people challenges denial, but adds only general creation support.
The command to find no disparity in the Merciful's creation provides a close structural parallel to its non-replacement.
The response to delayed rain does not clarify fitrah, orientation, or unchanging creation.
Revelation from the Creator of earth and high heavens offers only broad creator authority.
The distinction between sleep and death does not materially illuminate the focus.
Disbelief after a destructive wind is not a useful explanation of the focus.
Its recurring statement that most do not know is only a distant parallel in an punishment context.
Entering the Fire on the Day of Religion does not clarify the focus's upright religion.
The statement that Hell is a refuge adds no useful connection.
Divine clarification before misguidance offers a limited account of knowledge and responsibility.
The Originator of heaven and earth and varied creation support creator authority, but not the specific fitrah claim.
The criminals' despair at the Hour does not clarify the focus.
Following Abraham's hanif way is relevant but repeats the earlier Abraham material.
The sky's splitting does not contribute to the focus's central meaning.
The single straight path and the warning that many paths divide people directly explain the focus's one directed religion and the next ayah's sectarian contrast.
The companions' practical discussion after awakening does not clarify the focus.
The universal perishing of creatures does not explain the focus's stable created order.
Variation in provision is a same-surah sign but does not add to the focus after stronger cards.
Being gathered on faces toward Hell gives an inverse bodily image of orientation, but is too remote to add much.
The stages of human formation and loss of knowledge provide limited evidence of created human dependence.
The separation of two religions does not explain the focus's upright and exclusive religion.
God's knowledge of concealed and public speech does not materially clarify the focus.
Replacement with likenesses and a new formation concerns resurrection rather than the focus's unaltered creation.
Pharaoh's fear of expulsion from the land does not clarify the focus.
It joins creation of the earth with rejecting rival gods, supporting the focus's creator-based rejection of association.
The qualities promised the final abode do not explain the focus's central claim.
Changing spouses and retaining a gift uses replacement in an unrelated legal setting.
The Book's guidance and the absence of a guide after God's misguidance offer only broad support for right orientation.
Faces cast into the Fire give a distant inverse image of proper orientation.
Textual distortion and concealed disbelief do not materially explain fitrah or unchanging creation.
The greatness of an oath conditional on knowledge is not a useful connection.
Rules for distributing spoils and obeying the Messenger are outside the focus's subject.
The uniqueness of Iram's construction does not clarify divine creation's unchanging order.
Following ambiguous verses from inner deviation offers a distant contrast to stable, knowledgeable guidance.
It locates confusion about a new creation in people rather than divine incapacity, supporting the focus's rebuke of ignorance before the Creator's order.
It commands setting faces rightly and calling on God with sincere religion, closely extending the focus's commanded orientation.
It explicitly names changing God's creation as the satanic program, providing the clearest contrary boundary to the focus's no-replacement claim.
The primordial witness to God's lordship supplies a foundational counterpart to fitrah as an original human orientation toward God.
It joins sincere devotion, establishment of religion, prayer, almsgiving, and hanifiyyah in a concise parallel to the focus.
It commands following Abraham's upright hanif religion, directly reinforcing the focus's specified mode of orientation.
It rejects partisan religious identity in favor of Abraham's hanif way, supporting the focus's nonsectarian orientation.
It contrasts turning away from Abraham's religion with the chosen, submitting disposition associated with his way.
Submitting one's face to God while doing good closely parallels the focus's face-directed religious commitment.
Submitting the face to God and holding the firmest handhold gives a practical model of sustained upright orientation.
Worshipping God with religion made sincere clarifies the exclusive devotion implied by turning the face toward religion.
It declares pure religion to belong to God and rejects mediating partners, directly supporting the focus's anti-associative orientation.
The command to worship God with sincere religion restates the focus's exclusive religious direction in a worship setting.
The command to be the first to submit to the Creator reinforces creator-grounded religious allegiance.
Its declaration that religion with God is submission gives a concise doctrinal counterpart to the focus's upright religion.
It warns that a religion other than submission will not be accepted, clarifying the singular direction of the focus's religion.
Its appeal to inherited practice despite lacking knowledge sharply contrasts with the focus's creation-grounded religion and its diagnosis of ignorance.
It records reliance on forefathers' religion as guidance, supplying a direct contrary pattern to fitrah-based orientation.
It generalizes the defense of inherited custom against messengers, clarifying why the focus contrasts divine formation with widespread ignorance.
The soul's proportioning and subsequent moral discernment provide a close anthropological parallel to fitrah.
God's creating, proportioning, and balancing of the human person gives concrete content to an ordered original formation.
The pairing of creation with proportioning concisely supports the focus's account of a divinely established created order.
Creation of the heavens and earth in truth and the shaping of human forms offer broad support for a good divine formation.
God's shaping of people and making their forms good gives a secondary parallel to fitrah as a sound formation.
Its assertion that no change exists in God's established way supports the focus's no-replacement claim, though it concerns divine practice rather than creation.
